name: Genetic Central Nervous System and Retinal Vascular Disease

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Genetic CNS and Retinal Vascular Disease Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Identification of pathogenic mutation in associated gene(s) by molecular genetic testing
Presence of characteristic retinal vascular abnormalities confirmed by ophthalmological examination and fluorescein angiography
Clinical evidence of central nervous system involvement including stroke-like episodes or leukoencephalopathy on MRI
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant or recessive inheritance
Exclusion of acquired or other genetic causes of CNS and retinal vasculopathy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of pathogenic genetic mutation plus retinal vascular abnormalities and neurological manifestations
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of clinical, imaging, and genetic data.

searchTerms: blocked retinal arteries with small aneurysms
frequent transient brain blood flow problems
white matter brain changes on MRI

common.symptomName: Visual field defects due to retinal ischemia
searchTerms: vision loss in parts of visual field
headaches linked to brain vessel disease

laboratory: Genetic testing revealing pathogenic variants in CNS and retinal vascular genes
Normal routine blood tests excluding acquired vasculitis
imaging: Brain MRI showing confluent white matter hyperintensities consistent with leukoencephalopathy
Fluorescein angiography demonstrating retinal vascular occlusions and microaneurysms
genetic: Mutations in genes associated with hereditary small vessel disease and retinal vasculopathy (e.g., TREX1, COL4A1)
other: Family history consistent with inherited vascular disorder
Exclusion of autoimmune or infectious vasculitis

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of encephalopathy, branch retinal artery occlusions, and hearing loss
Distinct MRI findings with corpus callosum lesions

redFlags: Sudden onset of visual loss or field defects
Recurrent unexplained ischemic strokes in young patients
